explanation: A runner laps a circular track at a CONSTANT speed, yet the velocity is never constant. Speed is the scalar magnitude — how fast — and it stays fixed here. Velocity is the vector arrow, always pointing along the path (tangent); since the direction keeps turning, the velocity keeps changing even though the speed does not. The runner sweeps the circle at angular speed omega = v / R.
bullets: Speed is a scalar (just the magnitude); velocity is a vector with direction.
In circular motion the velocity is tangent to the circle and constantly re-aims.
Constant speed can still mean changing velocity — that turning is what acceleration is.
